title: Choose checks that matter
subtitle: Make tests answer user questions.
concept: Tests compare given inputs with expected results. Normal, boundary and failure coverage matter more than test count.
intuition: Opening an umbrella in sunshine does not establish how it handles rain and wind.
objectives: Choose normal, boundary and failure cases from acceptance criteria.
Report commands, results, coverage and remaining checks.

body.title: Start with acceptance cases
body.text: For creation, check ordinary text, whitespace, 80/81 code units, duplicate titles and capacity. Expectations come from requirements, not copying current function results. Fast data-rule tests complement browser checks of feedback, refresh, keyboard and narrow layouts.

body.title: Read one test first
body.text: This example uses Node's built-in test runner. test names a case; assert.equal compares values; assert.throws checks rejection. npm test runs node --test tasks.test.mjs. Start by explaining one test's input, expected outcome and purpose rather than learning every framework.

body.title: Do not let implementation and expected answer share a mistake
body.text: Recomputing the same algorithm in an assertion may repeat its error. Establish expectations with simple manual cases, before/after comparison or an independent method. When deleting the second duplicate title, inspect which record remains. Passing tests establish their cases, not all security, browsers and inputs.

formalDefinition.text: Tests compare given inputs with expected results. Normal, boundary and failure coverage matter more than test count.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: Choose normal, boundary and failure cases from acceptance criteria.
Check rules against independent expectations, then inspect browser interactions.
Report commands, results, coverage and remaining checks.

workedExamples.title: Read a blank-input test
steps: Inputs are an empty array, three spaces and an ID.
Expect addTask to throw a handled error.
The page must separately catch it and display feedback.
workedExamples.answer: It supports rejection by the data rule, not visible feedback. No page event or rendering was exercised, so browser acceptance is still needed.

workedExamples.title: A deletion test
workedExamples.problem: How can deletion of one duplicate title be checked independently?
steps: Create same-title records with IDs a and b.
Expect only a, with its original content and state.
workedExamples.answer: Compare the explicit remaining record, not just length 1. Otherwise deleting the wrong record might pass.

commonMistakes.claim: More tests always mean more reliability.
commonMistakes.correction: Repeating one path can hide omissions. Prioritize important behavior and boundaries.

commonMistakes.claim: AI-written tests mean verification is complete.
commonMistakes.correction: Run them and compare expectations with requirements.

practice.answer: Ordinary Learn Git; 80 accepted and 81 rejected; whitespace-only rejected.
solution: State an expected outcome for each.

practice.problem: Does length changing from 2 to 1 prove the correct item was removed?
practice.hint: The wrong one could be removed.
practice.answer: No. Check the remaining ID and content.
solution: Identity determines which item was deleted.

practice.problem: Do passing rule tests establish refresh persistence?
practice.hint: Did the test access browser storage?
practice.answer: No. These do not exercise app.mjs and storage. Add and refresh in the browser.
solution: Separate data functions from page integration.
Obtain evidence in the relevant environment.

practice.problem: How should an agent unable to run tests report?
practice.answer: State not run and why, give commands and expected behavior, and let you execute and record actual results. Do not claim passed.
solution: Existing test code is not successful execution.

learningCheck.question: Which is a good deletion test?
choices: Only check that the array shrinks
Check the intended remaining ID and original content
Only check the page did not crash
feedback: The wrong object might be deleted.
This matches the selected record's behavior.

steps.question: A pure-function whitespace test passed. What does it prove?
choices: The data rule rejects that input
feedback: This case does not cover every browser.

steps.question: A duplicate-title deletion test checks only length.
feedback: Do not remove allowed inputs to suit a weak test.

steps.question: Only Node tests were run. What report fits?
choices: Publish without looking at the page
feedback: This states what the checks support.
